sources.title: F. Hiai, Concise lectures on selected topics of von Neumann algebras
sources.locator: Complete author-hosted 159-page lecture-note PDF; §1.1–1.3 (PDF pp. 3–4), §2.1 (PDF pp. 10–16), including Lemma 2.1, Theorem 2.2, and Example 2.4.

contents.name: §1.1–1.2: bounded operators, operator topologies, commutants, and the double-commutation theorem

source_review.read_extent: Read §1.1–1.2 and checked the definitions and the three equivalent closure conditions in the double-commutation theorem.
source_review.supports: Supports the concrete algebra, commutant, WOT/SOT, and double-commutant conventions used on the A page.
source_review.limitations: The local bicommutant item supplies the finite-amplification argument explicitly and keeps the exact AC assumption.

contents.name: §1.3: predual and characterization of positive normal functionals

source_review.read_extent: Read §1.3, including the definition of M_* and the normal-positive criterion.
source_review.supports: Supports the predual and normality concepts in the local quotient theorem.
source_review.limitations: Hiai starts from the σ-weak predual; the local item proves its concrete trace-class quotient interface directly.

contents.name: §2.1: cyclic-separating vector and closability of S0 and F0

source_review.read_extent: Read the complete §2.1 argument establishing dense domains and closability from cyclic-separating data.
source_review.supports: Supports the Tomita-operator definition and commutant-pairing closability argument.
source_review.limitations: The local statement asserts only well-definedness, density, and closability for S0; no adjoint-core equality is imported.

contents.name: Lemma 2.1: polar decomposition identities for the closed Tomita operators
contents.reason: The later modular-data page owns the stronger Tomita identities involving J, Δ, inverse domains, and the fixed vector; this A page proves only the general polar calculus and closability.

source_review.read_extent: Read the complete lemma and its derivation from the polar decomposition of the closed operator.
source_review.supports: Identifies the modular identities required by the planned successor page.
source_review.limitations: Those identities are beyond the assigned A page and remain conditional on the later modular-data argument.

contents.name: Theorem 2.2: Tomita fundamental theorem
contents.reason: The commutant implementation and modular automorphism conclusions belong to the later modular-equilibrium page, not this prerequisite page.

source_review.read_extent: Read the theorem statement and the full proof in §2.1.
source_review.supports: Provides the exact later theorem boundary after the present closability and polar prerequisites.
source_review.limitations: No claim from this theorem is asserted by the assigned items.

source_review.read_extent: Read the finite-trace example following Theorem 2.2.
source_review.supports: Supports the use of a faithful trace and a standard Hilbert-space representation in the finite matrix example.
source_review.limitations: The local B example gives its own finite-dimensional Hilbert–Schmidt proof and does not infer the result for arbitrary algebras.

sources.title: Bruce Blackadar, Operator Algebras: Theory of C*-Algebras and von Neumann Algebras
sources.locator: Complete author-hosted 561-page book; Part I §§I.2.5.3–I.2.5.4, I.3.2.5, I.8.5.3–I.8.5.6, and I.9.1.1–I.9.1.2.

source_review.read_extent: Read the relevant commutant identities and finite-tuple double-commutant proof.
source_review.supports: Supports the imported strong/weak closure theorem used by the local bicommutant proof.
source_review.limitations: The local item independently writes out its finite-block projection step.

contents.name: Proposition I.3.2.5: bounded increasing positive nets

source_review.read_extent: Read the full proposition statement and proof outline, including the Cauchy–Schwarz estimate.
source_review.supports: Supports existence of a strong limit and least upper bound for bounded increasing positive nets.
source_review.limitations: The local proof constructs the limiting operator by quadratic forms and proves membership in M.

contents.name: §I.8.5.3–I.8.5.6: trace-class operators, trace norm, ideal property, and completeness

source_review.read_extent: Read the trace-class definition, the two-sided ideal estimate, and Banach completeness discussion.
source_review.supports: Supports the trace-class domain and norm estimates used in both local duality and the predual proof.
source_review.limitations: Blackadar does not replace the local rank-one/Riesz proof of S1(H)* = B(H).

source_review.read_extent: Read the cyclic/separating criteria and the adjacent standard representation argument.
source_review.supports: Supports the representation-dependent distinction between cyclicity and separatingness.
source_review.limitations: The local equivalence is proved directly with the projection onto closure of MΩ.

sources.title: Edward Witten, Notes on Some Entanglement Properties of Quantum Field Theory
sources.locator: Complete author-hosted 80-page text; §3.1, printed pp. 18–20 (PDF pp. 19–21), equations (3.1)–(3.10) and footnote 15.

contents.name: Equations (3.1)–(3.5): Tomita operator on the dense orbit and closed extension

source_review.read_extent: Read the operator definition, separating-vector well-definedness, and sequential graph extension.
source_review.supports: Supports the Tomita core and graph-closure context.
source_review.limitations: The local proof supplies its own commutant-pairing proof of closability under only the stated cyclic-separating assumptions.

contents.name: Equations (3.6)–(3.10): antilinear adjoint and polar decomposition

source_review.read_extent: Read the antilinear adjoint convention and polar factorization, converting Witten’s inner-product convention explicitly.
source_review.supports: Supports the need to define the antilinear adjoint before modular use.
source_review.limitations: The local definition uses linear-first inner products and reduces polar decomposition to a proved linear theorem.

contents.name: Footnote 15: the displayed calculation proves extension, not equality with S0*

source_review.read_extent: Read the complete footnote and its warning that the preceding argument establishes only an extension relation.
source_review.supports: Supports the local restriction against asserting an unproved adjoint/core equality.
source_review.limitations: No equality of S0* and the closure of the commutant Tomita operator is claimed here.

sources.title: Claire Anantharaman and Sorin Popa, An Introduction to II1 Factors
sources.locator: Complete author-hosted 338-page book draft; Chapter 7 §7.4, Theorem 7.4.5 and its proof (PDF pp. 119–121).

contents.name: Theorem 7.4.5: trace L1 identifies the predual in tracial standard form

source_review.read_extent: Read the theorem statement and complete proof, including trace norm, surjectivity, and dual identification.
source_review.supports: Provides an independent treatment of the trace-class/predual correspondence in a tracial standard representation.
source_review.limitations: Its scope is tracial von Neumann algebras; the local quotient proof establishes the concrete B(H) result for arbitrary represented von Neumann algebras.

sources.title: Edward Witten, Notes on Some Entanglement Properties of Quantum Field Theory
sources.locator: Complete author-hosted 80-page text; §4.1, printed pp. 32–34 (PDF pp. 32–34), equations (4.1)–(4.13), with the cyclic/separating criterion read in full.

contents.name: Finite bipartite standard representation: cyclic and separating criterion for tensor-factor algebras

source_review.read_extent: Read the finite-dimensional tensor-factor example and its complete-rank criterion for cyclicity and separatingness.
source_review.supports: Supports the finite-dimensional representation distinction illustrated on the B page.
source_review.limitations: Witten’s factor-algebra setting differs from the single defining M_n representation; the B item proves that case independently.

contents.name: Equations (4.4)–(4.13): finite-dimensional Tomita polar data
contents.reason: These finite modular-operator formulas are successor-page material; the current example stops after cyclicity, separatingness, and the vector functional.

source_review.read_extent: Read the finite-dimensional Tomita and polar formulas through equation (4.13).
source_review.supports: Marks the modular calculation that follows the finite cyclic-separating representation example.
source_review.limitations: No modular-operator formula is claimed in the assigned B item.

sources.title: F. Hiai, Concise lectures on selected topics of von Neumann algebras
sources.locator: Complete author-hosted 159-page lecture-note PDF; §1.3 and §2.1 (PDF pp. 4 and 10–11), plus the §1.9 overview standard-form paragraph on left multiplication in L2(M,τ) (PDF p. 9).

contents.name: §2.1: cyclic-separating vectors and GNS realization of faithful states

source_review.read_extent: Read the cyclic/separating definitions and faithful-state GNS realization.
source_review.supports: Supports the representation-specific vocabulary and vector-functional context.
source_review.limitations: The finite matrix counterexample and its faithful Hilbert–Schmidt vector are proved locally.

contents.name: §1.9 overview: standard form on L2(M,τ) by left multiplication

source_review.read_extent: Read the standard-form overview identifying left multiplication on L2(M,τ).
source_review.supports: Supports the Hilbert–Schmidt standard representation used for finite matrices.
source_review.limitations: The source passage is an overview for semifinite algebras; the item verifies the matrix case directly.
